title: What can a Unitree G1 or H1 humanoid lift on a house-building site?
summary: Whole-body static payload envelopes of the MuJoCo Menagerie Unitree G1 and H1: feet fixed, the combined centre of mass of robot and load kept over the feet, every joint inside its peak torque limit, and the load bisected at each hand height and reach. The G1 holds a median 4.5 kg in its palms (1.5–4.7 kg at 0.4–0.5 m forward, up to 12 kg close in), in line with Unitree's 2–3 kg arm rating, and its 50 N·m waist pitch is the usual limit. The H1 holds a median 14.2 kg, limited by its 18 N·m elbows. On nine residential tasks the G1 can carry a 2x4 and hold a nailer but not a 2x6. The H1 can take one end of a 4x8 OSB or drywall sheet with a person and set a lightweight concrete block, but not a whole sheet, a normal-weight block or a 60 lb bag, and neither reaches an 8 ft ceiling. Task masses are sourced (USG, NDS, a CMU survey, a nailer listing), and OSB is swept over 45–51 lb. Static only, at peak torque, with a pose that is not torque-optimal; not a rated payload.
lede: can a stock humanoid carry building materials? MuJoCo static payload envelopes of the Unitree G1 (median 4.5 kg, waist-limited; matches Unitree's 2–3 kg rating) and H1 (median 14.2 kg, elbow-limited): the G1 can carry a 2x4 but not a 2x6, the H1 can take one end of an OSB or drywall sheet with a person and set a lightweight block, but not a whole sheet, a normal-weight block or a 60 lb bag, and neither reaches an 8 ft ceiling.
